lesson_3.title: Bubble Sort Mechanics (Ascending)
task: Bubble Sort is an elementary sorting algorithm. It functions by iterating through a dataset, comparing adjacent elements, and swapping them if they reside in the incorrect order. This progressively forces the largest elements to 'bubble' to the end.
1. Execute an outer loop over the array to manage passes.

lesson_3.title: Selection Sort Mechanics (Ascending)
task: Selection Sort divides the array into sorted and unsorted partitions. It minimizes swaps by sequentially scanning the unsorted partition for the absolute minimum element, then executing a single swap to place it correctly.
1. Iterate via an outer loop `i`. Assume index `i` holds the minimum.
2. Scan all elements strictly to the right of `i` using an inner loop.
3. If a smaller element is detected, update the minimum index tracker.
4. Upon completing the inner scan, swap the newly found minimum element with index `i`.
2. Loop `i` from 0 to `length of arr`. Inside, set `min_idx = i`.
3. Nested loop: `j` from `i + 1` to `length of arr`. If `arr[j] < arr[min_idx]`, update `min_idx = j`.
4. Outside the inner loop, swap `arr[i]` and `arr[min_idx]`.
